The Dummy’s Guide to Coding for Minibus Taxis
event.description: Our company is Sebenza, and we have installed 5000 wifi routers in minibus taxis across South Africa to get internet into the hands of those that can scarce afford it. Along the way, we had to learn how to code for the minibus - that is, being able to work on the cheapest of phones, sometimes with limited signal, all running through complex custom firmware that run on routers. In short - we made so many early mistakes from our choice of stack, to our rollout approach and implementation, that this talk is an ode to what we figured out along the way, what technologies worked, and how we bent them to our will. This is, in fact, a coder's starter kit to building for the uniquely South African experience and its limitations and strengths. We won't spend too much time on the wide spectrum of material here, but rather framing this as a journey against sometimes-hostile tech and our own desperate attempts not to succumb to the growing dread that we were, in fact, Dunning Kruger sufferers.

event.title: State of the Developer Ecosystem - Insights from OfferZen’s Developer Nation Report
event.description: Jason Tame, Engineering Manager at OfferZen, will be unpacking insights from our State of the Developer Nation Report relevant to the Developer Ecosystem.

event.title: All the cool tech behind building a smart parcel locker network in South Africa
event.description: This talk uncovers the comprehensive journey of developing the hardware, microcontroller firmware, cloud infrastructure, web-based software, IoT network, and mobile app for a growing worldwide trend in ecommerce logistics: smart parcel lockers. Discover how we used technology to overcome some of the unique challenges to South Africa around security, load shedding, network coverage, logistics, costs and consumer behaviour.

event.title: Turning Doubters Into Believers - Bringing Flash to the Enterprise and Beyond
event.description: No one believed us. At every corner we were told no one needs the performance of Flash, and even if you did, it will be too expensive for the Enterprise at scale, so don't bother to change. "My last migration will be onto Pure? I don't believe you!" "No way you can do non-disruptive hardware and software upgrades with no performance loss on a Tuesday morning!" "Data Reduction is black magic, I don't trust it!" "It can't be that simple..." This is how we did it; from the 'knife fights in phone boxes' in the early days to giving back weekends to Storage Admins, to seeing the delight in our customer's faces when all of our promises came true. "It does what it says on the box!" Fast forward to 2024 and Pure Storage is quietly powering the most demanding workloads for the most critical IT infrastructure in the South Africa. So what does the future hold? Find out in this session...

event.title: Ducking Duck - Rubber Duck 2.0 : Building an AI powered robot rubber duck.
event.description: Come with me on a journey as I attempt to totally revolutionise rubber ducking and build the ultimate rubber ducking companion. Using all of the latest buzz-word compliant AI technology including voice recognition, large language models, machine vision and robotics I attempt to build the ultimate debugging companion. This isn't just a frontend to ChatGPT this is a bespoke, offline, secure debugging companion that will revolutionise your debugging and also become your friend. The talk covers the dead-ends, the ups and downs as I try build something a little smarter than your Alexa/Siri and a little cuter than your typical rubber duck. Whether you're interested in AI, Robotics, Rubber Ducks or just the struggles of integration hell there will be something in this talk for everyone.

event.title: The science of queues: Performance monitoring theme parks (and distributed systems)
event.description: Performance monitoring is an important part of running a successful theme park. Like a distributed system, theme parks have separate components (attractions). Each has a queue in front of it. How can we find out which of them are the least efficient? Which ones are slowing us down? Where should we spend time optimizing? Join me for a roller-coaster ride through distributed system performance monitoring. Find out which measurements tell you the most about your system and how to optimize it. As an added bonus, you'll learn how to run a successful theme park!

event.title: How building a portable escape room made me a better developer
event.description: I built a portable IoT escape room, and it changed how I think about development! In this session, we'll uncover unexpected parallels between escape rooms and architecting resilient, scalable systems. Let me share the lessons learned, and how they translate into invaluable guidance for Domain-Driven Design (DDD), modularity, communication, scalability and fault tolerance. Doors will be unlocked at the end - even if the audience can't solve the puzzles.

event.title: Rewriting a datastore, at millions of transactions per second
event.description: After the AWS impact in Dec 2021 many teams had to take action. This talk follows a two-plus year project in which we re-architected the backing data store for one of the most widely used diagnostic tools in EC2, the distributed log tracer. We look at how this service impacted EC2 in the December event, in terms of our own delayed recovery, and delays caused to EC2 recovery. We consider the scale of the problem being solved (we write trillions of records every day, and read only a very small fraction of them), and then we work through why it took us over two years to get the new solution into production and delighting customers. Including completely changing certain design decisions due to latency issues, and finding "that one weird bug" multiple times.

event.title: From Phone Calls to Function Calls: My Journey from Call Centre Agent to Frontend Lead Developer
event.description: Listen to a captivating narrative that unfolds the inspiring journey of a self-taught Frontend Lead Developer who began in a South African village and now flourishes in Berlin's tech hub What's in it for you? This isn't just a story; it's a source of motivation and a testament to the power of perseverance. Witness a "struggles to successes" tale for the digital age This narrative offers more than inspiration; its a reminder that every obstacle is an opportunity, and every setback is a setup for a comeback. It's a journey that promises to ignite your own aspirations and leave you with a renewed belief in the potential within you Join in to explore the incredible transformation that unfolds when an ordinary individual like you harnesses determination, resilience, and a boundless thirst for knowledge to conquer the ever-evolving world of software development. Be prepared to be inspired, motivated, and equipped with the knowledge that your own journey to success is just waiting to begin

event.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Cross-Platform: Insider Stories of Mobile Development
event.description: Dive into the world of cross-platform mobile app development through the lens of firsthand experiences with 'The Good, the Bad, and the Cross-Platform.' This talk will unravel the complexities and nuances of using various cross-platform tools, drawing on real-life stories from the trenches of development. Discover the pitfalls to avoid, the unexpected victories, and the lessons learned along the way. Whether you're deciding on a framework for your next project, looking to streamline your development process, or simply curious about the cross-platform landscape, this presentation will arm you with the insights needed to navigate the challenges and opportunities of building mobile apps that stand the test of device diversity.

event.title: A World Without Passwords? Are We There Yet?
event.description: Passwords are the bane of my existence, and I'm sure they're yours too. We're constantly burdened with creating complex passwords, forgetting them, resetting them, and eventually settling for something simple (and weak), leaving us vulnerable to account takeover attacks from credential spraying and phishing. As developers, we have the power to rid the world of passwords and provide better authentication experiences for our users. Passwordless forms of authentication exist, but they're flying under the radar due to a lack of awareness and education. It's time to shine a light on them. In this talk, you'll learn about the existing forms of passwordless authentication (webAuthn + passkeys), and leave with knowledge of how you can start adopting them into your products.

event.title: P-AI-R Programming with Gemini
event.description: During this talk attendees will get first-hand experience developing an application (either .NET 8 and/or Node.js) using Visual Code with Gemini. We are starting out from a basic project (provided via my public GitHub repository) and are going to "discuss" matters, refactor and extend the application with Gemini, our AI-based assistant. P-AI-R programming, or programming with AI-based assistants, is a new paradigm for software development that leverages the power of AI to help developers write better code, faster. Gemini is a Google Cloud service that provides AI-powered assistance for developers, including code completion, code generation, code understanding, and code refactoring.

event.title: Building Yourself an AI Powered Microscope
event.description: Are you fascinated by the prospect of assembling your own intelligent Digital Microscope, writing the control software for it and deploying it from the cloud? If the answer is yes, then this session is for you! The other title for this talk could have been "How I solved my own accessibility problems with tech and AI". What started as a mobile app project to read the part numbers on integrated circuits has transformed to become a Raspberry Pi Linux based kiosk app, Digital Microscope powered by AI Vision. The reason for this: it's becoming increasingly hard for me to read the text on IC's (without a magnifying glass). The ONLY solution to this accessibility issue is ofcourse with technology and electronics!!! Imagine building your own Microscope that can read text, identify objects, and gain insights from the visuals. We could call this "Copilot for Microscopes"! Join me for a fun "Do-it-yourself" session with demos and code!

event.title: 10 Lessons I Learned About Engineering Leadership from Ted Lasso
event.description: This talk goes into the ten lessons which Benny learned from the Emmy Award Winning show Ted Lasso, about an American Football coach hired to coach an English Football (soccer) team. Benny applied the Lessons as a consulting Head of Engineering for a HealthTech with some moderate success. Please be aware that there are tons of Spoilers.

event.title: Tech's Secret Superpower: How to Unleash Neurodiverse Talent
event.description: Join me as I walk you through my story as an autistic engineer in the software industry, and how we can reap the rewards of undeniable neurodiverse talent by applying inclusive strategies from the hiring process to the workplace. While neurodiversity may sound like a modern buzzword, we’ll delve into this definition and attempt to demystify it. You will gain awareness of the difficulties that neurodiverse people experience in the industry, and learn suggestions for changes that can prevent difficulties in future. Let’s unleash the superpower of neurodiverse tech talent: my advice on embracing neurodivergent coworkers will be essential for all roles in the industry, as well as for neurodiverse individuals in the audience who may resonate with my stories, and use these key tips as inspiration for what they may implement in their careers.

event.title: Making observability tangible (with end-to-end test automation)
event.description: The tooling for observability (metrics, traces, logging) has been evolving at a rapid pace. The benefits this offers are remarkable but it is hard to see the potential without practical experience. On smaller projects (or projects in their infancy) it is also hard to get enough traffic to have statistically meaningful data to showcase observability benefits. I will give a brief introduction to the terms and tools available and will point out some common pitfalls when starting out with collecting metrics. In the more interactive part of the talk I want to show how end-to-end tests can be used to continuously instrument a sample application to establish a baseline of observability data. This can then be used to help us get a better understanding of the inner workings of our application and to diagnose problems created during the talk.

event.title: If it's everywhere, why aren't you using it?
event.description: WebAssembly. Wasm. Wat. What? What?! It's everywhere, in the browser, on the server, embedded devices, your preferred runtime. Every. Where. Why should you start to take note? How can Wasm be a cohesive force, allowing you to use the best tools for the job, yet still remain portable and performant. Rust, Zig, Go, Python and friends can all work together using WebAssembly. We've heard it before, but what does it mean in practice? What does this unlock, for you, the developer? Let's see how Wasm can make you more productive, open up new possibilities and allow contributions from many different disciplines to come together and form the solutions we need for modern challenges. I will share lessons learned in bringing together various development efforts to build a solution that would be a serious challenge to do with only one or two programming languages or frameworks.

event.title: Developer Driven-Testing: ship better code faster by removing the testing column.
event.description: Have you ever written some code and thought to yourself "I suspect there are still bugs in here, but I can’t say where exactly. Let's see what they find during testing..." Increasingly, high-performing teams are making developers primarily responsible for testing throughout the software development lifecycle. There is no hand-over to another person to write tests or perform testing activities before code can be released. In this talk I’ll explain what Developer-Driven Testing (DDT) is and how it can lead to higher code quality, and faster development cycles. However, it’s not as simple as just deleting the testing column - I’ll cover the steps needed to get to that point. I’ll share some practical examples on how to improve the effectiveness of your tests - something that is critical when operating without a testing phase as a safety net. And what about the role of quality engineers in teams that do DDT? Come and find out how DDT enables them to provide even more value to teams.

event.title: Non-Functional or Dysfunctional? Don't Leave Quality to Chance
event.description: I am so tired of "Obviously". It's too late for "Obviously". I never want to hear "Obviously" again. In a world where non-functional requirements are left to chance, a lone developer bravely confronts software quality. He sighs deeply. Obviously our app needs four nines reliability. Obviously it must respond within 200 ms. Obviously a toddler should find it easy to use. Obviously it should scale to 100 000 users. Obviously it must repel attacks from Anonymous... There's nothing obvious about any of this! We think we can fulfil these requirements at no cost, but we can't. We think they'll just emerge, and we're disappointed. We never define quality attributes well enough. Not across the board. If we're deliberate about performance and security, we neglect modifiability and availability. Why do we do this? Again and again... Is it too late? Or can one intrepid developer lead us to a safer place? One iteration at a time. Never to be bullied with "Obviously" again...

event.title: Building on a Crypto Operating System
event.description: Cryptocurrencies are here to stay, and playing a key role in modernising and innovation in the financial sector. Did you know that you don't need to be a big business or a blockchain expert to start building that next generation financial system, for yourself? In this session, we'll be taking a practical look at how to build on top of VALR's world-class API, going from 0 to 1 with running code, as well as discuss a range of build possibilities.

event.title: I Can't Believe It's Not Native!
event.description: The web's come a long way, baby! The gap between the web and native platforms has been closing for years, and it's finally gotten really small. It used to be that web applications did not have access to a lot of mobile platform functionality, but did you know that you can access Bluetooth, NFC, USB directly from a web app, and that iOS Safari finally supports web push notifications? Even with the new platform capabilities of the modern web, you may still be concerned about performance! Aren't web browsers slow? I'll cover how you can build UIs that look and feel just as slick as a native UI. Of course, there are no silver bullets, so I'll also discuss when the web is not a good choice, and you might prefer to go native.

event.title: Death to the Server : The New Serverless Era
event.description: For my 40-minute talk on "The new serverless era", I will offer an informative and educational exploration of serverless computing. I'll begin by introducing key concepts and delve into the advantages of serverless, addressing potential challenges and mitigation strategies. I'll demonstrate the practical aspects of developing and deploying serverless functions on Azure and AWS, providing a simple code example and sharing best practices for monitoring and debugging. Additionally, I'll discuss security considerations and best practices while showcasing a real-world case study to illustrate the technology's practical application. This talk is designed to inform and educate the audience about serverless computing

event.title: How modern computers play board games
event.description: Bao (or Bawo) is a mancala type game originating out of east Africa. It is an old and somewhat obscure game with little to known records of its origins. It has become an obsession and is a wonderful game to illustrate how computers can play board games. This talk will be about the algorithms that computers use to play board games (Like chess, go or Bao) and finally will apply what was learnt to make the best engine for Bao that could likely beat almost any human player.

event.title: Data Science For Dummies
event.description: The Data Science buzz is reaching new heights and it seems like a pretty intimidating field and set of tools. This session utilises a live demo to walk through the basic concepts of Data Science. It makes the case for why you should learn Data Science tools and how you can get started today!

event.title: Chains Redefined: Blockchain’s Promise for Africa’s Rich Resources
event.description: In a world where the term 'chains' often conjures images of restriction, "Chains Redefined" explores the liberating power of blockchain technology in managing Africa's natural wealth. This talk is a journey for everyday software developers, a journey from historical chains of exploitation to modern chains of opportunity and innovation. It’s an exploration into how blockchain, a technology many developers interact with daily, can have profound impacts far beyond cryptocurrency – specifically in revolutionizing the management of Africa’s rich resources.

event.title: Module Federation: Your teams don't need to deploy together
event.description: A deep dive into Webpack Module Federation and what it can do for you, your teams and your monolithic frontends. Deploy separately but still present one application to the user, you can have good developer experience and user experience at the same time.

event.title: Kids coding on Space Stations 🛰️ and Robots 🤖... volunteers needed! 🫵
event.description: Join us at DevConf for a dual showcase that’s sure to inspire! In a groundbreaking session, we’re thrilled to present two trailblazing groups who are not just shaping the future of technology, but also embodying the spirit of innovation. Coder LevelUp: With a visionary target to empower 500,000 coders in the Western Cape, Coder LevelUp is revolutionizing the tech landscape. Their mission? To transform the region into a vibrant hub of digital expertise. Textpand: Meet the world-renowned FIRST Tech Challenge champions hailing from Cape Town. Textpand isn’t just a team; they’re pioneers, setting the global standard for competitive tech excellence. But here’s the twist – the masterminds behind these technological marvels are none other than students! That’s right, these young geniuses are still navigating the halls of school while simultaneously steering the wheel of technological advancement. This session is more than a display of cutting-edge technology; it’s a celebration of the youthful passion and intellect driving it. Discover the origins of these remarkable initiatives and explore how you can contribute to a movement where technology serves the greater good.

event.title: Delve into the Dungeons of Cybersecurity at DevConf 2024!
event.description: Join us on a quest as we unveil the mysterious connection between continuous performance enhancements and the emergence of 0-Day Exploits. As the clock struck midnight on December 31st, 2023, a frantic call summoned our Paladin to confront a lurking terror within our system's depths. Prepare your spells and sharpen your swords as we journey into the heart of darkness, where 0-Day Exploits lie in wait, ready to ensnare the unwary. Witness the treacherous exploits of the past, from the V8 JavaScript engine's betrayal of Google Chrome to the sinister schemes that plagued Apple iOS. Venture forth into the nexus between performance and security, where every enhancement risks awakening the dreaded Tarrasque of vulnerability. Learn the invaluable lessons of vigilance and adaptation as we navigate the perilous landscape of software development. Join the Q&A to share insights and seek guidance. Together, let's conquer the darkness for cybersecurity excellence.

event.title: From Complexity to Clarity: Navigating Microservices with Kubernetes
event.description: In today's dynamic software development landscape, adopting microservices is key to achieving greater scalability, flexibility, and faster innovation. While the benefits of microservices are clear, they come with their own set of complexities. Successfully implementing a microservices architecture extends beyond breaking down applications; it demands a thorough understanding of deployment, management, and observability. The prevalent adoption of the "You Build It, You Run It" philosophy marks a significant shift towards developer accountability and empowerment. As a modern developer understanding the platform your applications run on, is not just beneficial, it's essential. We invite you to a technical session tailored for forward-thinking developers ready to tackle the challenges of deploying microservices using Kubernetes. This session is focused on demystifying the deployment platforms that will house your applications, emphasizing the early adoption of practices such as logging, tracing, monitoring to name a few. The session will cover:Preparing Your Development EnvironmentCrafting Docker ImagesApplication Deployment with KubernetesMonitoring and Troubleshooting Techniques within KubernetesSecurity Measures and Best PracticesExploring Advanced Features of Kubernetes

event.title: Co-creating API Banking
event.description: Discover how Investec's developer community is shaping the future of API banking and Programmable Banking card accounts. Learn about the collaborative efforts that are enabling developers to craft bespoke financial solutions, drive rapid innovation, and seamlessly integrate banking services into diverse digital ecosystems. This masterclass will showcase the synergy between technology and finance, highlighting the collective intelligence of a thriving developer community. Wayne Summers (Head of Open APIs at Investec) - The Story of Programmable Banking Wayne will share the journey of Investec's programmable banking, its vision, and the impact it has on the financial industry. Devin Pearson (Investec Developer Community member) Hands-on with the Investec API: Programmable Banking Card Accounts and Community Projects Devin will provide a technical walkthrough of the Investec API, demonstrating real-world applications and community-driven projects. Attendees are encouraged to bring their laptops to follow along. Nick Benson (Developer Community Lead @ Investec) The Pulse of Investec's Developer Community Nick will discuss the ethos of the Investec developer community, its role in fostering innovation, and how new members can get involved.

event.title: Protecting Kubernetes Workloads: A Developer's Guide with Veeam Kasten K10
event.description: Overview of Kubernetes and its significance as a platform for running code.Introduction to K10 and its role in Kubernetes data management and protection.Importance of protecting Kubernetes environments and the role of K10 in achieving this.Deploy 1st Application to Kubernetes:Walkthrough of deploying an application onto a Kubernetes cluster.Explanation of key concepts such as pods, deployments, and services.Create Initial K10 Policy to Protect App:Demonstration of setting up K10 policies to protect the deployed application.Explanation of backup strategies, retention policies, and disaster recovery configurations.Kubernetes Perform Backup & DR:Hands-on exercise on performing backups and disaster recovery operations using K10.Practice restoring applications and data in case of failures.Application & Code Mobility:Discussion on strategies for application and code mobility within Kubernetes environments.Exploration of tools and practices for seamless migration and scaling of applications.

event.title: PRQL: a modern language for transforming data - a simple, powerful, pipelined SQL replacement
event.description: The past 50 years have seen a great evolution in programming languages — except in the world of databases. There, SQL still reigns supreme; but is it a shark, enduring due to its perfection, or a dinosaur, one impact away from extinction? We argue that SQL is an amalgamation of both: relational algebra — the shark; and the language — the bloated dinosaur. PRQL incorporates the beauty of relational algebra while also embracing the best from libraries like dplyr, Pandas, and LINQ to name just a few. It is a functional, pipelined query language with modern ergonomics and expressivity that compiles to SQL, making it usable on any relational database. PRQL is open source, contributor-driven, and committed to staying that way forever. This talk will motivate why we need a modern query language to replace SQL, introduce PRQL, and demonstrate its elegance and productivity as a language for data using interactive examples. Join us and learn about the latest evolution in query languages!

event.title: Navigating the Storm: Tools and Patterns for Resilient Systems in the Face of Production Chaos
event.description: Troubleshooting large, distributed systems during production outages can be a daunting challenge. When downtime is not an option, how do you steer your ship through the storm of technical difficulties? Drawing from extensive experience trying to keep production up at one of South Africa's largest banks, this talk delves into the realm of resilience engineering. It will equip you to identify and reproduce issues and also to make your systems more resilient in the face of chaos. We will explore an array of troubleshooting tools, such as Application Performance Monitoring tools, logging, heap and thread dumps, application metrics, profiling techniques, load testing, and briefly touch on chaos engineering. Recognizing that prevention is better than cure, we will conclude with patterns and strategies to help you build resilient systems. Topics will include timeouts, connection reuse, circuit breakers, bulkheads, and fallback mechanisms.

event.title: From Overheating to Overachieving: A Comedic Tale of Hacking My Car
event.description: Embark on a humorous and enlightening journey into the world of car hacking in this developer-focused conference talk. As my trusty old car overheated and befuddled multiple repair shops, I decided to take matters into my own hands. Armed with an OBD connector, I ventured to uncover the secrets hidden within my vehicle's systems. In this presentation, I'll guide you through the process of reverse engineering, offering a brief Electronics 101 for beginners. Discover how I used Arduino to decode the mysterious signals on the car's CAN bus. Along the way, I'll share my humorous misadventures and the lessons learned from my escapades. But the journey doesn't stop there. I'll also explore the exciting possibilities that car hacking opens up. Learn how a friend transformed his gasoline car into an electric marvel using the same techniques.

event.title: So you want to be a CTO
event.description: Most technical people reach a point in their career journey where they must decide between management or remaining in an individual contribution role. At the same time, many good technical people believe the only way to advance their careers is by taking on a role in management. In this talk, I will cover two critical aspects of the CTO role. Firstly, is it a good career choice for you Secondly what are the skills and attributes required to succeed in the CTO role?

event.title: Container-based development in a Corporate Network
event.description: Supporting developers inside a corporate network has many pitfalls. How can we leverage containers to share environments, simplify deployments and manage vulnerabilities centrally?

event.title: Embracing Neurodiversity in the Software Industry
event.description: Neurodiversity refers to the range of differences in how individuals cognitively process the world around them. Neurodiversity is an umbrella term that includes (but is not limited to) autism spectrum disorders, ADHD, dyslexia, dyscalculia, and Tourette's disorder. Individuals with these differences make up a large portion of the population and it is found that the software industry seems to be an attractive industry for individuals with these differences, therefore it is imperative to embrace this population to better understand their differences, the strengths that they bring to the table, and the common difficulties that they may face in a workplace setting.

event.title: Will AI really take my job? - A Call for Complete Developer Mindshift!
event.description: AI is changing how we develop software. AI tools can generate, complete, debug, optimize, and review code. But how do you use them effectively and responsibly? How do you enhance your creativity and productivity, without losing your identity and autonomy as a developer? In this session, you will learn about the current state of AI tools for software development, and how they can help you at distinct stages of your career, which may include. - Starting off as a newbie developer - Increasing your confidence as a junior developer - Delivering higher quality work after a promotion to senior developer You will also discover the challenges and opportunities of working with AI as a co-creator, and how to adopt a new mindset that embraces AI as a partner, not a competitor. Join me, as we walk through a new world of AI and developers co-existing to accelerate innovation through short demos on AI code generation/ completion tools, debugging and documentation tools and code review tools.
